name: pi-agent
_comment: ONE CONFIG FOR THE WHOLE AGENT, in the same paradigm as a template spec.
Before this, running a cell meant a docker line with nine flags, repeated in
e2e.sh, bench.sh and by hand — and every one of them was a place for the node
id, the bucket or the endpoint to drift apart. A cell is not a container and
should not be launched like one; this file is what celldctl.mjs reads, and it
is the only place any of it is written down.
`target` picks where the same config runs:
local     celld in docker against MinIO — what the tests use
platinum  the real thing: templates from spec, sandboxes, the org's bucket

cell._spec: The IMAGE. celld and nothing else — the agent is not in it.
_node: STABLE and unique per org fleet. celld routes a cell to its owner BY NODE
ID: a node that returns with a fresh identity is not the owner and every
request answers DurableObjectRoutingError until the old lease expires.
Under Platinum the host derives this from the sandbox id; run it by hand
and you have to say it yourself.
_memory_mb: HARD CAP on the celld container, and the reason is not tidiness.
celld keeps cells resident until memory pressure (CELLD_IDLE_EVICT_S is
disabled by default), so a few hundred sessions grow without limit. On a
16 GB laptop that OOM-killed the Docker VM mid-suite, repeatedly, which
then looked like a bug in whichever claim was running at the time.
celldctl also sets CELLD_MAX_RSS_MB to 80% of this, so celld sheds cells
itself instead of being killed: a shed cell is a cold start, a killed node

workspace._spec: Generated from daemon/server.js by `npm run spec`. Never edit it.

_config: The agent bundle's own configuration — bindings, new_sqlite_classes,
string vars. celld reads this file directly during `celld deploy`.
Shipping new agent code writes to the BUCKET; it does not rebuild an
image, and it does not reach a cell that is already running.

_image: Which celld the LOCAL target runs. Set to pt-celld:0.4.0 to test the newer
one; ../pt-celld.spec.json is what Platinum actually builds and still pins
The difference is not cosmetic. MEASURED, by flipping a marker in the worker
0.3.0  60s, still the old bundle. `celld --help`: 'Nodes load a deployment
at startup; restart them to serve this version.'
0.4.0  adopted after ~20s, no restart. Its help: 'A running node polls the
deployment pointer and adopts the new version in place; nothing
So RUNBOOK.md's 'a redeploy does not reach a running cell' is true of the
pinned version and false of the next one.

_comment: PLATINUM ALREADY HAS AN OBJECT-STORAGE STORY, and this uses it rather than
inventing a second one. The variable names are the canonical ones from
apps/api/src/s3.ts — the module that exists because casGC.ts, reconciler.ts
and api/sandboxes.ts had each grown their own copy of this block and had
already drifted. A fourth copy here would be the same mistake.
THE PREFIX IS NOT OURS TO CHOOSE. A cell's namespace is orgs/<org_id>/,
and hosts/host-agent/.../cell_s3_gateway.go cellS3Prefix() calls itself
'the one place an org's storage namespace is decided' — derived from the
sandbox row, never from anything the guest sends. The host mints the
sandbox its own scoped S3 identity and points CELLD_ENDPOINT at the on-host
gateway, which holds the provider key. So a cell never receives AWS_*, and
deploy-time tooling must not pin a prefix the platform owns.
See ../CREDENTIALS.md: passing raw AWS_* in envVars hands the sandbox the
whole bucket, which is exactly what that gateway exists to stop.
platinum._prefix: The FLEET prefix from s3.ts, not the org namespace. orgs/<org>/ is appended by the host.

_comment: WHICH PROVIDERS ARE COMPILED INTO THE BUNDLE. Measured, not guessed:
slim  3 APIs      2051 KB   first cell ~116 ms
all   39 providers 2819 KB   first cell ~127 ms   (default)
768 KB and 11 ms apart, and that cost is per NODE, paid once: a second cold
cell is 34 ms either way. 36 extra providers for 11 ms is why `all` is the
default rather than a careful minimum.
slim is not three vendors, it is three APIs: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
(OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, Together, Fireworks, Cerebras, xAI, Azure, a
local gateway) works under either set with provider 'openai' and base_url.
With no api_key the cell runs the scripted model, so tests need no
credentials and cost nothing.
_auth: openai-codex authenticates with a CHATGPT SUBSCRIPTION, not an API key:
its auth record is {oauth: {name: "OpenAI (ChatGPT Plus/Pro)", isSubscription: true}}.
Log in once, in this directory:
That writes auth.json HERE (the CLI resolves it relative to the cwd).
celldctl reads it automatically; auth.json is gitignored.

_comment: WHICH TOOL BACKEND the cell uses.
platinum  the platform own sandbox API (/exec, /files, /files/list,
/files/grep) with a sandbox:<id>-scoped key. sandboxScope.ts:
"a key confined to ONE sandbox and its children, so you can hand
an agent running inside a sandbox a credential that cannot touch
the rest of the org." That is this, already built.
daemon    the standalone HTTP service in daemon/. For local runs where
there is no control plane to call.
Selection is by PRESENCE of PT_API_URL + PT_SANDBOX_KEY + PT_WORKSPACE_ID,
not by this field: a deployment that has a scoped key must not keep talking
to a daemon that is not there.
